# Lambda Refactor Lab
<!-- Slide 57 -->

## Can Lambdas Shorten This Program Without Changing It?

The roster program works. Make it shorter and clearer with standard algorithms and lambdas, without changing a single character of its output.

::: notes
Slides 58–61

The program checks its own output against the original every time it runs. That check is the test: any refactor that makes it fail is wrong, however good the code looks.
:::

<!-- Slide 58 -->

---

## How to Run the Lab

Lab files: [refactor_lab_prompt.md](assets/refactor_lab_prompt.md){target="_blank"} and [roster_loops.cpp](cpp/roster_loops.cpp){target="_blank"}

1. Copy roster_loops.cpp into main.cpp in Replit and click Run. The last line should read "Output check: PASS."
2. Paste the prompt and your program into an AI assistant.
3. Replace main.cpp with the AI's program and click Run.
4. If the check says FAIL, it shows the first line that differs. Find the job that printed it and fix it yourself before asking the AI again.
5. Audit every lambda with the checklist. Fix what it flags, then click Run again.

::: notes
Students work in Replit without a shell. The bottom of the file holds the original output and a checkOutput function; main captures the program's output and compares it line by line, printing PASS or the first line that differs. The prompt tells the AI not to touch main or the check.

Instructor answer key: assets/refactor_lab_answer_key.md. Reference solution: cpp/roster_lambdas_reference.cpp.
:::

<!-- Slide 59 -->

---

## Audit Checklist

- Is every capture named, rather than `[=]` or `[&]`?
- Is each capture by value or by reference for the right reason?
- Is each Student parameter `const Student&`, or `Student&` only when the lambda changes the student?
- Is every find_if result checked against end before it is used?
- Does every comparator use `<` or `>`?
- Was any loop forced into an algorithm it does not fit?

::: notes
The last question is the trap. The letter-grade tally computes five results in one pass and should stay a loop. AI tools often convert it to for_each with [&] capturing five counters, or to five count_if calls. Both pass the output check, and both fail the audit.
:::

<!-- Slide 60 -->

---

## Report Back

- Which loop did you keep, and why?
- Which capture or parameter did you change, and why?
- What did the AI get wrong?

::: notes
Collect two or three answers to the last question from the room. The point of the lab is that a refactor passing its output check is not finished until a person who understands the rules has checked it.
:::
